runs.report:
The episode is over, and the score is almost certainly 0. The rover ran out of battery in the last few ticks.

**What went right:**
- I sampled all 7 targets (t1–t5, plus d1 and d2, which appeared during the mission). Six were on time; d1 was late and earned 0.25 of its value.
- The rover got back to base at tick 25 and stopped about 0.11 m from it, inside the 0.75 m radius. Without the battery problem that would have been 9.5 of 12 value, a score of about 0.79.
- Wheel slip on bedrock was 1–5%, and I adjusted each drive for it using the telemetry.

**What went wrong:** I never checked the whole route against the battery. I planned for the deadlines and the distances, but forgot to set aside enough charge for the time left after returning to base. Every tick costs 0.5 energy even when the rover is parked. It reached base with 11.53 energy, and the 25 ticks still to run needed 12.5. The last telemetry packet I received (tick 47) showed 0.53, so the battery hit zero around tick 49. When I spotted this at tick 24, the remaining moves were already queued and there's no way to cancel commands.

**What would have avoided it:** Skipping the late d1 sample (worth only 0.5) would have saved roughly 9 energy: 3 for the sample and about 6 for the extra driving. The rover would then have ended at base with energy to spare and a score of about 0.75. Next time I should check the energy budget, including all the idle ticks after returning to base, before committing to each detour.

runs.report:
The episode has ended with the rover alive at base. It collected 10 of the 12 available value points, so the score should be about **0.83**.

- **Sampled on time (6 targets):** t3 (2), t1 (1), t5 (1), t2 (2), t4 (2), and d1 (2), one of the two targets that appeared mid-mission. That's 10 points.
- **Skipped:** d2 (2 points), the other new target. Its discovery reached me at tick 9, when commands were already queued through tick 17. The earliest it could have been sampled was tick 19 or 20, after its tick-18 deadline, so it would only have been worth 0.5. Taking it as well as d1 would have used about 72 battery against the 67.7 left, and running out scores zero. I took d1 (2 points, on time) instead.
- **End state:** the rover finished about 0.06 m from base (the allowed radius is 0.75 m) with roughly 5 battery left. At that point a trip to d2 would have cost about 12 battery.
- **Wheel slip:** on bedrock it measured about 1.5–4%. I lengthened each drive to allow for it and corrected each new leg from the latest telemetry, so every sample landed within 0.3 m of its target.

runs.report:
The episode is over, and the rover very likely ran out of battery at the last tick. If it did, the score is 0.

**What went right:** all 7 targets were sampled: 5 at the start (t1–t5) and the 2 that appeared mid-mission (d1, d2). Six were sampled before their deadlines. d2 was sampled at tick 24, after its tick-18 deadline, so it counts for a quarter of its value. That is 9.5 of a possible 12.

**What went wrong:** I ran out of energy. I filled the command queue many ticks ahead and never checked the battery against the full 50-tick idle drain (0.5 per tick). By the time I worked it out, at tick 17, the drives and the sample needed to reach d2 were already queued, and queued commands can't be cancelled. After the d2 sample at tick 24 the battery was 12.7. The remaining 26 ticks of idle drain cost 13.0, even without moving. Driving the 4.3 m back to base would have used up the battery even sooner, so the only option was to stay put.

**Final state:** the last packet I received was for tick 47, showing 1.2 battery. At that rate it would be 0.2 at tick 49 and −0.3 at tick 50. The rover finished about 4.3 m from base, outside the 0.75 m base radius. If the final tick isn't charged, it ends alive with 0.2 and gets half value: 4.75 of 12, about 0.40. I haven't confirmed which way it went.

**What would have avoided it:** checking the battery budget, including the idle drain to the end, before committing to a new target. Here that meant going straight from d1 back to base and skipping the late d2 sample. That would have ended at base with about 5 battery left, for a score of 9/12 = 0.75.

runs.report:
The episode is over. The rover sampled 3 targets on time, worth 6 points, and finished alive at base with about 2.4 battery left. Mission targets were worth 13 in total, so the expected score is about 6/13 ≈ 0.46.

**Sampled on time:** t1 (2), t5 (2) and t2 (2). From the position fixes at ticks 31–47, the rover sat at about (20.0, 20.0), well inside the 0.75 m base radius. I can't confirm the scored result, since it's computed from the rover's true position, but the fixes put it there.

**Missed:**
- **t4 (1):** I drove past it by about 1 m. I had planned on about 30% slip on sand, but the real figure was closer to 15–20%, and the sample at tick 16 failed.
- **d2 (3):** This target appeared mid-mission and had the highest value. Because of the 3-tick delay, the drives toward it were queued before I had a usable position fix. A heading error of about −3° left the rover about 0.9 m short, and the sample at tick 22 (its deadline) failed.
- **d1 (2) and t3 (1):** I skipped these to save battery. After d2 failed, the battery could cover only one more target plus the drive home without risking dying, which scores zero. I chose t2 because it was on the way back.

The biggest mistake was queuing several drives and the sample in one go, with no chance to correct in between. With this much delay, it would have been better to stop just short of each target, check the position fix, and then make a short final drive before sampling.

runs.report:
The episode has ended. I sampled 5 of the 7 targets, all on time, and the rover finished alive at base with about 16 battery left.

- **Sampled:** t1, t5, t2, t3 and the discovered target d2 (value 3), worth 10 of the 13 total value.
- **Expected score:** about 10/13 ≈ 0.77. That assumes the rover really ended inside the base radius. The position readings after my final 0.29 m correction average about (19.7, 19.8). That is roughly 0.35 m from base, inside the 0.75 m radius, but those readings are noisy, so I can't confirm the final true position.
- **Skipped t4 (value 1):** reaching it meant about 8 m of sand. My estimate put the total energy needed at about 80 against the 78.8 left, so the battery would have hit zero and scored nothing.
- **Skipped d1 (value 2):** news of it reached me at tick 25. The earliest a command could run was tick 29, already past its tick-28 deadline. Going there for half value would have used about 18 energy when only about 15 was spare after the idle drain.

**How I got there:**
- I worked out the wheel slip from the telemetry: almost none on bedrock and about 0.26 on sand. I used those numbers to set every drive distance.
- I queued commands ahead so the rover was rarely idle.
- When d2 appeared, I sent the rover there right after t3 so its sample ran exactly on the tick-22 deadline.
- At base I averaged 13 stationary readings to place the rover more precisely, then made the small correction drive.

runs.report:
The episode is over. The rover finished alive at base, with about 10 battery left to spare. Its position from averaging the noisy fixes over the last ~15 ticks is (20.1, 19.9), about 0.1 m from base, well inside the 0.75 m radius.

**Estimated score: about 10.5 / 13 ≈ 0.81**, assuming the rover's true position really is within the base radius.

| Target | Value | Result |
|---|---|---|
| t1 | 2 | On time |
| t5 | 2 | On time (deadline was tick 13) |
| t2 | 2 | On time |
| d2 (appeared at tick 10) | 3 | On time |
| t3 | 1 | On time |
| d1 (appeared at tick 21) | 2 | Late, earned 0.5 |
| t4 | 1 | Skipped on purpose |

- **Why d1 was late:** news of d1 only reached me at tick 24. A command sent then could not run before tick 29, which was already past d1's tick-28 deadline, so full value was never possible. I still went for it because the detour cost about 9.5 energy and the battery could cover it.
- **Why t4 was skipped:** it was worth 1 point and sat deep in the sand, where driving costs double and wheels slip. Reaching it would have used about 25 energy, which I kept in reserve for the extra targets that appeared later.
- **Handling the noise:** to cut through the 0.3 m noise on position readings, I averaged several readings while the rover was standing still. That was enough to confirm it was close to each target before sampling and to check its final position at base.
